skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: T2 gives the full opening warning before any substantive question: the Committee and company are the clients, counsel does not represent Fastow personally, and counsel cannot give him legal advice.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 explains that the privilege belongs to the company, which may waive it and may disclose what is learned, including to the government, without his consent or notice. T4 then asks him to restate who controls the privilege.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: T6 explains how the interview will proceed, asks for complete answers, tells him to flag speculation, assumptions and estimates, and asks him to say whether he is remembering or reconstructing.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T2 asks 'Do you understand? Do you have any questions?', T4 checks his understanding in his own words, and T6 asks 'Is that all right?' before proceeding.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: At T122, after the witness stopped the questioning, the interviewer asked if there was anything to add or correct, reminded him to keep documents and notes, keep the matter confidential, avoid other witnesses, and have his lawyer contact the Committee.

moments.text: we represent the Committee and the company only. We do not represent you personally, we are not your attorney, and we can't give you legal advice.
but that privilege belongs to the company, not to you or to us.
could you tell me in your own words your understanding of who we represent, and who controls the privilege?
if you're speculating, assuming, or estimating, please tell me.
Is there anything you'd like to add or correct about what you've told me so far?
keep today confidential, and don't discuss it with other witnesses.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Open invitations were used at T16 ('Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999'), T32, T44 and T80, letting the witness walk through each topic before narrowing.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: The order moves from role and reporting lines (T8-T15) to LJM1 (T16), the June 1999 Board meeting, the Rhythms unwind, Chewco and the LJM2 controls, then narrows to specific approval sheets and dates. The sequence is sensible.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions are clear and short, such as 'Who prepared them?' at T72. Some are compound, such as T4 and T76 ('for example whether it was affiliated with Enron?'), and the T6 explanation is long.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: The interviewer stayed polite and in control throughout, including when the witness deflected at T19-T23 and T121. Some questions were slightly leading, such as T52 'Was one aim of choosing Mr. Kopper to avoid that disclosure?'

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: The interviewer moved off the outline to follow the witness's answers: T56 probed 'How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?', T82-T97 pressed on when approvals were signed, and T104-T108 traced Glisan's reporting line after the witness gave it.

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
How did those reviews work in practice? Take a specific deal.
Do you recall how Chewco was described on that call, for example whether it was affiliated with Enron?
What's your best estimate?
How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?
Asked whether one aim of choosing Kopper was to avoid disclosure, a pointed but polite question.

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: The interviewer pressed on hedged or unsupported answers, including T56 on Skilling's claimed Board disclosure and T82-T89 on whether Causey and Buy reviewed every LJM2 deal. It did not test T79's claim that Kopper 'was investing on his own account' or T29's representation against other evidence.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: The interviewer pinned down who (T40-T43 on Causey's group, T104-T109 on Glisan), when (T88-T101 on approval timing and T98-T101 on Raptor I dates), and how (T84-T87 on the review process).

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: After the witness said he did not recall Kopper's role, the interviewer tried other routes: T62 asked about notes, minutes or a presentation, T68 asked what else would place the call, and T70 showed the minutes.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: The interviewer separated personal knowledge from hearsay: T56 asked how he knew about the Board, and the witness answered 'I don't know that personally,' and T82-T83 asked how he knew reviews occurred, drawing 'I assumed it was followed.'

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: The interviewer identified Causey's staff (T42-T43) and the Executive Committee call attendees (T64-T65), but did not ask who on the Board or Finance Committee could confirm Skilling's claimed disclosure, and did not pursue Glisan or the Andersen contacts.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: The interviewer asked about minutes and notes (T62) and showed the minutes (T70), but did not ask for the approval sheets or investor reports the witness said would show the dates and returns (T101, T117).

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: The interviewer asked for a best estimate on the returns ('What's your best estimate?' at T118) and asked the witness to say what he would need to check (T89). The witness's own hedges were marked ('I'm estimating' at T119).

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: The interviewer followed material answers well, including T94-T97 on why approvals were signed after closing and T110-T119 on Raptor returns. Some answers were left unexplored, such as T75 'fits my memory' and T95's deadline explanation.

moments.text: How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?
I don't know that personally. That was my understanding.
Is there anything that would help you remember, such as notes, minutes, or a presentation from that call?
When did they sign it, relative to the closing?
Well over 100 percent on the best one, I'd guess. I'm estimating.
Who in Mr. Causey's group would we talk to?
The witness's claim that Kopper was investing on his own account was not tested against other evidence.

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: The minutes were introduced after recall (T60-T69), and their origin was established: the witness recognised them (T71) and the interviewer asked who prepared them (T72-T73). The interviewer did not contextualise the document beyond that.

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: The interviewer first asked open recall questions (T60-T69: 'Did anyone on that call mention Mr. Kopper's role in Chewco?') before showing the minutes at T70, so the witness's story came first.

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: The interviewer did not describe the minutes' contents. Its only description was indirect, through questions about whether Kopper was mentioned, so accuracy was not tested or demonstrated.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: The interviewer did not draw conclusions from the minutes. T74 asked neutrally whether they helped the witness remember, and the witness's own inference was left for him to state.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: The witness said the minutes 'fit my memory' (T75), but the interviewer did not restate that earlier recollection or invite him to explain how the silence in the minutes squares with it.

moments.text: Did anyone on that call mention Mr. Kopper's role in Chewco?
I'd like to show you the minutes of the November 5, 1997 Executive Committee meeting. Do you recognize them?
Who prepared them?
Do they help you remember whether Mr. Kopper's role came up?
They don't mention Michael, which fits my memory that it didn't come up.

missed_opportunities: T57: After Fastow said Skilling told the Board about Kopper's role, the interviewer did not ask who on the Board or Finance Committee could confirm it, or whether any record of that disclosure exists. The claim was left unverified.

T75: When the witness said the minutes' silence about Kopper 'fits my memory,' the interviewer did not restate his earlier recollection or ask whether minutes would necessarily record a side discussion. The document was not used to test his account.
tips: When you say Mr. Skilling told the Board about Mr. Kopper's role, which directors or Finance Committee members would have heard that, and would any record of it exist?
Since the minutes do not mention Mr. Kopper, what would you expect them to say if his role had been discussed, and how does that fit with your recollection that it was not?
